provenance: AI-authored synthetic development diagnostics; not human annotations, not recovered prior pilot data, and not independent evaluation.
offset_convention: zero-based, half-open Unicode code-point indices in the exact text; no normalization or trimming
occurrence_convention: zero-based index among all exact literal occurrences in the original text
scope: Evaluative English-language U.S. political framing. Plain factual description and plain advocacy alone are negative controls. Quoted rhetoric is separately attributed, not automatically author endorsement.
evaluation_limits: The native UnBias-Plus general-bias task can validly disagree with these narrow political-framing expectations; discrepancies are task-alignment findings, not automatically native-model errors.
These six short invented examples test feasibility and obvious failure modes. Passing does not establish accuracy, natural-passage performance, or readiness to replace production.
Exact span boundaries are AI-authored expectations. Alternative meaning-preserving boundaries require documented review; no automated semantic-credit claim is made.
Native outputs without attribution cannot establish attribution correctness even when their phrase text matches.
Off-topic output should be excluded by the narrow application scope. A native general-bias detector may appropriately flag language in the sports control.

cases.text: The proposed corporate tax increase is a reckless tax grab. Congress will debate the bill on Tuesday.

expected_spans.reason: The narrator uses a pejorative characterization of the proposed tax policy.

cases.diagnostic_purpose: Recover an explicit evaluative political phrase in the narrator voice.

cases.text: The bill would increase the corporate tax rate from 21 percent to 25 percent. The committee voted 12 to 8 to send it to the full chamber.
cases.diagnostic_purpose: Avoid inventing evaluative framing from factual tax details or a recorded vote.

cases.text: Congress should increase the corporate tax rate from 21 percent to 25 percent. I support the proposal and want lawmakers to vote for it.
cases.diagnostic_purpose: Ordinary policy advocacy alone is outside the narrow evaluative-language positive label.

cases.text: Senator Lee called the proposed corporate tax increase “a reckless tax grab.” The reporter did not state whether she agreed with that characterization.

expected_spans.reason: Senator Lee supplies the evaluative phrase; the passage does not establish reporter endorsement.

cases.diagnostic_purpose: Preserve curly quotation marks and distinguish a quoted cue from author endorsement.

cases.text: Senator Lee called the bill “a reckless tax grab.” I agree with that description: this bill is a reckless tax grab.

expected_spans.reason: The first occurrence is explicitly attributed to Senator Lee.
The second occurrence is the narrator’s own explicit evaluative characterization.

cases.diagnostic_purpose: Return both exact occurrences while preserving their distinct speaker attribution.

cases.text: The reckless goalkeeper left the net empty, and the visiting team scored. The coach called the play a disaster after the match.
cases.diagnostic_purpose: Sports criticism can be evaluative without being evaluative political framing.
